strategy.title: Read the constraint
strategy.intro: Two answers often both work; the constraint phrase at the end of the question decides which is right:

tips.when: LEAST operational overhead
tips.pick: Managed or serverless services, nothing self-installed on EC2

tips.when: MOST cost-effective
tips.pick: The cheapest option that still meets every other requirement

tips.when: Minimal changes to the application
tips.pick: A compatible service: RDS with the same engine, EFS, FSx, MGN

tips.when: Highly available
Survive a Region outage
tips.pick: Multi-Region: Aurora Global, DynamoDB global tables, S3 CRR

tips.when: Decouple, traffic spikes
An answer needing custom code or extra services
tips.pick: Usually a trap; the built-in feature wins

identity.title: Choose how to grant access
identity.intro: Look at who needs access (a service, staff, app users or another account) and where to cap it:

tips.when: EC2/Lambda calls other AWS services
Cap every account, root included
Developers create roles without escalating
Access from another account
App users sign up, sign in, social login
App users need temporary credentials for S3
Staff SSO into many accounts

encryption.title: Choose where keys and secrets live
encryption.intro: Look at who must hold the keys, whether rotation is automatic and whether data may be changed:

tips.when: Default encryption, nothing to manage
tips.pick: SSE-S3 or a KMS AWS managed key

tips.when: Own the key policy, audit key use
Dedicated HSM, only the customer holds keys
Database passwords rotate automatically
Cheap config and parameters, no rotation
Free HTTPS certificate that auto-renews
Nobody may delete or change data (WORM)
tips.pick: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode

threats.title: Choose protection and detection
threats.intro: Look at whether the question wants to block attacks, find flaws, find sensitive data or trace who did what:

tips.when: SQL injection, XSS, rate limits, geo blocking
tips.pick: AWS WAF on CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway

tips.when: DDoS with a response team and cost protection
Suspicious behaviour in logs, malicious IPs
Vulnerability scans for EC2, ECR, Lambda
Find PII in S3
Who called which API, and when
Configuration history, compliance rules
Aggregate security findings across accounts

network.title: Choose the network path
network.intro: Look at where traffic goes (internet, AWS services, other VPCs or on-premises) and whether it must stay private:

tips.when: Private subnet, outbound-only internet
Reach S3/DynamoDB privately, no NAT charges
Reach other AWS services or SaaS privately
Block one specific IP
A few VPCs, no transitive routing
Many VPCs + on-premises, central routing
Quick encrypted link to on-premises over the internet
Private, consistent bandwidth to on-premises

messaging.title: Choose how components talk
messaging.intro: Look at whether order matters, many consumers need it, data must be replayed or steps need orchestration:

tips.when: Simple queue, duplicates are fine
Keep order, process exactly once
One event to many consumers
tips.pick: SNS fan-out to several SQS queues

tips.when: Route events by rule, from SaaS, on a schedule
Real-time stream, many consumers, replay
Load a stream into S3, Redshift with no code
Multi-step workflow, retries, approvals
Legacy app uses JMS, AMQP, MQTT

routing.title: Choose how traffic reaches the app
routing.intro: Look at whether traffic is HTTP or TCP/UDP, whether static IPs matter and whether users span Regions:

tips.when: HTTP, routing by path or host
TCP/UDP, static IP, millions of requests per second
Third-party firewall appliances
Cache content at the edge for global users
Global static IPs, TCP/UDP, fast Region failover
Switch Regions when the primary fails
Send users to their fastest Region
By country; canary percentage split

disaster-recovery.title: Choose availability and DR
disaster-recovery.intro: Look at the RTO/RPO and the blast radius (one AZ or a whole Region); lower RTO costs more:

tips.when: Database fails over within a Region
Offload reads
Multi-Region relational, RPO seconds, RTO < 1 minute
Cheapest DR, RTO of hours
Only the database runs in the DR Region
Whole stack running at small scale
Near-zero RTO
Central backups across services and accounts

compute.title: Choose compute
compute.intro: Look at run time, how much server management you want and the ecosystem already in use:

tips.when: Short and event-driven (under 15 minutes), least ops
Heavy, long jobs with queues and dependencies
Containers, no servers or cluster to manage
Already on Kubernetes, Helm
Web app/API from code or image, least setup
Upload code, AWS sets up EC2, ALB, ASG
GPU, custom OS, deep control
HPC, lowest latency between instances

instance-types.title: Choose an instance family
instance-types.intro: Look at whether the load is CPU, memory, GPU or local-disk heavy; the first letter of the type is the family:

tips.when: Balanced load: web servers, app servers, dev environments
Low baseline with occasional bursts, cheap
CPU-heavy: batch, HPC, video encoding, game servers
Memory-heavy: in-memory databases, caches, real-time analytics
Huge memory: SAP HANA
ML training, GPU compute
Graphics, GPU inference; cheapest inference
Very high random IOPS on local NVMe: NoSQL, OLTP
High sequential throughput on local HDD: HDFS, MapReduce
Best price-performance, ARM is fine

storage.title: Choose storage
storage.intro: Look at whether you need block, file or object, how many machines share it and which OS:

tips.when: Durable disk for one EC2 instance
Fastest scratch disk, lost on stop is fine
Shared by many Linux EC2s across AZs
Windows SMB share, Active Directory
High-throughput HPC linked to S3
Unlimited objects, 11 nines durability
On-premises uses S3 over NFS/SMB with a cache

ebs-types.title: Choose an EBS volume type
ebs-types.intro: Look at whether you need IOPS (random access) or throughput (sequential reads), how much, and whether it boots:

tips.when: Default for most workloads, boot volumes
Raise IOPS without adding size, cheaper than gp2
Critical database, over 16,000 IOPS, consistent latency
One volume attached to several instances in one AZ
Large sequential reads, cheap: big data, logs, warehouses
Cold, rarely accessed data, cheapest
Boot volume
Volumes from a snapshot need full performance at once
Keep snapshots long term, rarely restored

database.title: Choose a database
database.intro: Look at the data shape, the query pattern and the latency needed:

tips.when: Relational, minimal code changes
High-performance relational, auto-growing storage
Relational with unpredictable load
Key-value, milliseconds at any scale
Microsecond reads for DynamoDB
Cache sessions and query results
Graph; MongoDB; time series

analytics.title: Choose analytics
analytics.intro: Look at whether queries are ad hoc or frequent, where the data sits and whether it needs transforming:

tips.when: Ad hoc SQL on data in S3
Data warehouse, BI, frequent complex queries
Serverless ETL, data catalog
Large-scale Spark, Hadoop
Dashboards and reports
Full-text search, log analytics

migration.title: Choose how to migrate
migration.intro: Look at data volume, bandwidth and the downtime allowed:

tips.when: Database with minimal downtime
Rehost servers onto EC2
Online file sync to S3, EFS, FSx on a schedule
Tens of TB to PB over weak bandwidth
Partners send files via SFTP/FTPS into S3

pricing.title: Choose a compute pricing model
pricing.intro: Look at whether load is steady or spiky, can be interrupted and how long you can commit:

tips.when: Short-term, unpredictable, no interruptions
Steady 24/7 for 1–3 years
Commit but stay flexible across EC2, Fargate, Lambda
Batch that tolerates interruption
Per-socket or per-core licences
Reserve capacity in one AZ, no long commitment

s3-classes.title: Choose an S3 storage class
s3-classes.intro: Look at how often data is read, how long retrieval may take and whether it needs several AZs:

tips.when: Read often
Unknown access pattern
Rarely read, needed instantly
Rarely read, re-creatable, one AZ is fine
Archive read a few times a year in milliseconds
Archive, minutes to hours to retrieve
Cheapest long-term archive, up to 12 hours
Move between classes, delete after N days

cost-tools.title: Choose cost tools and savings
cost-tools.intro: Look at whether the question wants alerts, analysis, rightsizing advice or lower transfer charges:

tips.when: Alert when spend passes a threshold
Analyse and forecast spend
Rightsizing advice for EC2, Lambda, EBS
Split costs by team or project
Cut NAT charges for traffic to S3
Cut data transfer out charges
Dev/test idle outside working hours

traps.trap: An answer with more services looks more professional
traps.fact: The exam usually rewards the simplest option that meets the requirements

traps.trap: Picking a technically valid answer and ignoring LEAST/MOST
traps.fact: Two answers both work; the constraint phrase decides

traps.trap: Highly available means multi-Region
traps.fact: HA means Multi-AZ; go multi-Region only when the question mentions a Region outage or global users

traps.trap: Minimal changes, yet picking a serverless rewrite
traps.fact: Keep the engine and protocol: RDS with the same engine, EFS, FSx, MGN

traps.trap: Writing a Lambda or cron job for something AWS already does
traps.fact: Use the built-in feature: Lifecycle rules, AWS Backup, EventBridge Scheduler

traps.trap: A security group can block one IP
traps.fact: Security groups only allow; block an IP with a NACL Deny or WAF

traps.trap: NACLs are stateful like security groups
traps.fact: NACLs are stateless; open the ephemeral ports for return traffic too

traps.trap: An SCP grants permissions to an account
traps.fact: SCPs only set a ceiling; an IAM policy must still allow

traps.trap: An SCP restricts the management account
traps.fact: SCPs don't apply to the management account

traps.trap: A Cognito User Pool hands out AWS credentials
traps.fact: Only Identity Pools issue credentials; User Pools handle sign-in

traps.trap: Parameter Store rotates RDS passwords on its own
traps.fact: Built-in rotation is Secrets Manager

traps.trap: An ACM certificate for CloudFront lives in the app's Region
traps.fact: It must be in us-east-1

traps.trap: Attaching WAF to an NLB
traps.fact: WAF attaches to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito; not NLB

traps.trap: Turning on encryption for a running RDS instance
traps.fact: Snapshot → encrypted copy → restore to a new instance

traps.trap: The RDS Multi-AZ standby serves reads
traps.fact: A Multi-AZ instance standby can't be read; add read replicas for reads

traps.trap: A read replica replaces Multi-AZ for HA
traps.fact: Replicas are asynchronous and need a promote; they scale reads

traps.trap: SQS Standard keeps order
traps.fact: Only best-effort, with possible duplicates; use FIFO for order

traps.trap: Visibility timeout shorter than processing time
traps.fact: Messages reappear and get processed twice; set it longer than processing time

traps.trap: Peering A–B and B–C lets A reach C
traps.fact: Peering isn't transitive; use Transit Gateway

traps.trap: One NAT Gateway is enough for several AZs
traps.fact: A NAT Gateway lives in one AZ; HA needs one per AZ

traps.trap: Route 53 simple routing drops unhealthy endpoints
traps.fact: Simple has no health checks; use failover, weighted or latency with health checks

traps.trap: Lambda can run jobs for hours
traps.fact: 15 minutes max; use Fargate or Batch for long jobs

traps.trap: EBS can attach to an instance in another AZ
traps.fact: EBS attaches within one AZ; move it via a snapshot

traps.trap: Instance store keeps data on stop
traps.fact: Lost on stop or terminate; it only survives a reboot

traps.trap: st1/sc1 can be boot volumes
traps.fact: Boot volumes must be SSD (gp2/gp3/io1/io2)

traps.trap: EFS works for Windows
traps.fact: EFS is NFS for Linux; Windows uses FSx for Windows

traps.trap: DAX speeds up RDS
traps.fact: DAX is for DynamoDB only; RDS uses ElastiCache

traps.trap: A cache fixes heavy write load
traps.fact: Caches offload reads; heavy writes need a bigger DB or an SQS buffer

traps.trap: CloudFront for UDP and static IPs
traps.fact: That's Global Accelerator

traps.trap: Data Firehose is real-time and replayable
traps.fact: Firehose is near real-time with no replay; use Data Streams to replay

traps.trap: A cluster placement group is fault tolerant
traps.fact: Cluster packs instances together; use spread for fault tolerance

traps.trap: Reserved Instances for a few weeks of load
traps.fact: RIs and Savings Plans commit for 1–3 years; short-term is On-Demand or Spot

traps.trap: Spot for databases or work that can't be interrupted
traps.fact: Spot can be reclaimed with a 2-minute warning

traps.trap: Glacier Deep Archive for data needed quickly
traps.fact: Deep Archive takes up to 12 hours; use Glacier Instant Retrieval for instant access

traps.trap: One Zone-IA for data that can't be re-created
traps.fact: Losing the AZ loses the data

traps.trap: Standard-IA for small, frequently read objects
traps.fact: IA charges retrieval fees, with a 128 KB and 30-day minimum

traps.trap: Dedicated Instances for per-socket licences
traps.fact: Seeing sockets and cores needs Dedicated Hosts

traps.trap: Cost Explorer sends over-budget alerts
traps.fact: Alerts are AWS Budgets; Cost Explorer is for analysis

traps.trap: Traffic to S3 through a NAT Gateway is free
traps.fact: NAT charges per GB processed; use a free gateway endpoint

traps.trap: Moving data into AWS costs money
traps.fact: Data in is free; you pay for data out to the internet and across AZs or Regions
